A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AnchorWeave. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and matchable despite extensive reformatting and added supplementary analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, component ablations, camera-control measurements, and qualitative generation experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these results and adds runtime measurements, rendering diagnostics, and quantitative long-horizon stress tests.

M1.justification: Local memories, coverage-driven retrieval, Algorithm 1, multi-anchor attention, pose-guided fusion, and training objectives remain unchanged. Initial-anchor selection and character masking already appear in v1 Appendices B and F. The monitor extension in v2 H.3 is presented prospectively, without establishing a change to the implemented method.

E1.justification: RealEstate10K, DL3DV, and the existing open-domain static and gaming scenarios are retained. v2 adds an explicit reflective-surface failure case in H.4/Figure 13, broadening the tested scene conditions. Longer sequences and additional initial images primarily change evaluation design.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark, camera-control, and free-form comparisons retain their comparator membership and baseline descriptions. New efficiency and stress tests reuse SPMem. LiveWorld is discussed as a complementary approach, not evaluated as an additional baseline.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark protocols remain unchanged. New protocols include 20 initial images with repeated 80-frame exploration and 80-frame return phases through 2400 frames, revisit PSNR against the initial image, controlled history-fusion rendering tests, and runtime/memory evaluation on an RTX PRO 6000 with Wan2.2-5B at 81×480×832.

E4.justification: v2 adds history-dependent runtime analysis, a controlled diagnostic of rendering degradation under global fusion, repeated-revisit stress testing, and a reflective-surface failure study in Appendices G–H. These substantially extend the original memory, fusion, attention, and retrieval-count ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. The new 20-image sample and repeated camera cycles describe evaluation design rather than stochastic replication or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the camera-control table retain identical values. New results include 275 seconds/39 GB for K=4 in Table 4, long-horizon PSNR decay and SPMem rendering failure around frame 1120 in Figure 10, and rendering degradation from 44.83 to 16.15 dB in Figure 9. H.1 inconsistently prints 44.93 for that initial value.

T1.justification: The diffusion objective, mathematical setup, and greedy retrieval algorithm are retained. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations appear; the added scaling and robustness explanations are empirical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: replacing fused global memory with local memories, coverage-driven retrieval, multi-anchor control, and improved consistency and visual quality. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: New Appendices H–I substantially qualify applicability through accumulated synthesis errors, pose drift, view-dependent reflections, unreliable geometry in unfamiliar scenes, and backbone-limited inference speed. v2 also explains the runtime-quality trade-off and distinguishes static spatial memory from dynamic object-state tracking.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents 16×–32× point-cloud downsampling, camera-control primitives, scene-dependent step magnitudes, four-frame stationary phases for memory updates, and runtime hardware/resolution. These expand implementation disclosure; the PDFs do not establish changes to the retained generation procedure.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially broadens cited literature across camera control, dynamic view synthesis, and memory/caching approaches, including PostCam, See4D, AnyView, Flow Caching, and WorldCompass. H.3 additionally positions AnchorWeave as complementary to LiveWorld's dynamic memory. The closest-work distinction from SPMem, Spatia, and MagicWorld remains.

P1.justification: Existing prose is selectively condensed and clarified, with an added process-visualization subsection, revised appendix headings, numeric citations, and affiliation/acknowledgment updates. Most original paragraphs and the main narrative sequence remain recognizable; the scientific additions do not constitute wholesale rewriting.

P2.justification: The two-column main paper becomes single-column, substantially resizing and relocating figures and tables. v2 adds the efficiency table and Figures 8–13. Its main-text Figure 6 redisplays and annotates part of v1's appendix visualization; all original figure imagery is retained. Figure 2's caption also clarifies the visibility coloring.

improvement.justification: v1's long-horizon evidence chiefly comprised qualitative examples up to 241 frames. v2 adds a 20-image, 2400-frame quantitative stress test, computational scaling measurements, and concrete failure analyses, substantially strengthening assessment of the paper's central long-horizon claims and practical limits. Uncertainty estimates remain absent, and Table 4 does not clearly reconcile its Wan2.2 runtime setting with quality values matching the CogVideoX ablation, but these reporting limitations do not outweigh the substantial evidential gains.
